q: A risk assessment identifies a threat with high impact but very low likelihood. Mitigating it would cost substantially more than the expected loss. Which risk response is MOST appropriate?
c: Accept the risk and document the decision
Transfer the risk through insurance
Mitigate the risk regardless of cost
Ignore the risk since likelihood is low

q: A development team is threat modeling a new payment service and wants a structured way to enumerate potential threats against each element of the data-flow diagram. Which approach BEST supports this goal?
c: Apply STRIDE categories to each data-flow element
Score each known vulnerability using CVSS
Commission an external penetration test
Review the enterprise risk register entries

q: An internal document states that all company laptops MUST use AES-256 full-disk encryption. Compliance is mandatory and no exceptions are listed. Which type of document is this?
c: A security standard
A security policy
A security guideline
A security procedure

q: During an internal audit, a CISSP-certified analyst discovers that a colleague has been falsifying vulnerability scan results to hide missed remediation deadlines. What should the analyst do FIRST?
c: Confront the colleague privately and ask them to stop
Report the findings through the organization's internal channels
File an ethics complaint with ISC2 against the colleague
Escalate directly to the external audit committee

q: A US-based SaaS provider hosts and processes EU customer personal data strictly on the instructions of its European business clients. Under the GDPR, how is the provider classified?
c: As a data processor
As a data controller
As a data subject
As a supervisory authority

q: An organization is beginning its business continuity program. Management wants to know which business processes and systems must be recovered first after a disruption. Which activity provides this answer?
c: A quantitative risk assessment
A disaster recovery test
A business impact analysis
A threat and vulnerability assessment

q: A manufacturer learns that a vulnerable open-source library may be embedded in firmware delivered by several of its third-party suppliers. Which practice gives the organization the BEST visibility into this exposure?
c: Signing non-disclosure agreements with every supplier
Increasing the frequency of internal code reviews
Purchasing cyber insurance covering supply chain incidents
Requiring a software bill of materials from each supplier

q: An online contract platform must ensure that a customer who electronically signs an agreement cannot later credibly deny having signed it. Which security concept is the platform enforcing, and what typically provides it?
c: Authenticity, provided by validating the customer's login credentials
Nonrepudiation, provided by digital signatures over the agreement
Integrity, provided by hashing the agreement after signature
Accountability, provided by recording the signing in an audit log

q: A data center asset valued at $400,000 has an exposure factor of 25% for a flood that historical records show occurs about once every 10 years. What annualized loss expectancy (ALE) should the risk analyst report for this threat?

After purchasing a cyber insurance policy covering ransomware losses, a CFO tells the board that the ransomware risk 'is now the insurer's problem.' What should the CISO clarify about this risk treatment?
c: The risk has been avoided, so the organization no longer needs ransomware-specific controls
Part of the financial impact is transferred, but accountability and uninsured impacts such as reputational damage remain with the organization
The risk has been fully mitigated because insurance operates as a compensating control
The risk has been accepted, because a premium was knowingly paid in place of deploying controls

q: Ahead of an acquisition, a security director commissions research into the target company's breach history, audits its control environment, and reviews its outstanding regulatory findings before integration begins. Which principle is the director demonstrating?
c: Due diligence
Due care
The prudent person rule
Compliance management

q: A CISSP consultant discovers that a client's water-treatment control system has a safety flaw that could endanger the public. The client, who pays the consultant's fees, instructs them to omit the finding and tell no one. Under the ISC2 Code of Ethics, why can the consultant not simply comply?
c: The canon to advance and protect the profession forbids concealing findings from fellow practitioners
The canon to act honorably requires the consultant to resign the engagement immediately
The duty of diligent and competent service to principals requires disclosure directly to the client's regulator
The canons are applied in priority order, and protecting society and the public trust outweighs duties owed to the client

q: A multinational plans to consolidate all HR records into a single cloud region in the United States. Counsel warns that several countries where employees reside have data localization statutes. What is the MOST significant risk-management implication for the consolidation plan?
c: The plan automatically violates GDPR because HR records are special-category personal data
Some employee records may be legally required to remain in-country, so the design must support per-jurisdiction storage or lawful transfer mechanisms
Under the cloud shared responsibility model, cross-border compliance obligations shift to the provider hosting the data
Encrypting the records in transit and at rest satisfies localization requirements because plaintext never leaves the country

q: An employee's suspected data theft could lead either to termination under HR policy or to criminal prosecution. The CISO asks why the investigation approach must be decided early. What is the BEST answer?
c: Criminal cases use the preponderance-of-evidence standard, so less rigorous collection is generally acceptable
Administrative investigations require law enforcement involvement from the outset
A criminal case demands proof beyond a reasonable doubt, so evidence handling must meet the strictest standard from the outset
Civil and criminal matters cannot arise from the same underlying incident, so a single path must be chosen now

q: A financial regulator opens an inquiry and formally demands five years of transaction logs. The operations team notes that the retention policy requires only three years, though older logs still exist on backup tapes. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Issue a legal hold suspending routine destruction of all potentially responsive records, including the tapes
Destroy the logs older than three years because the retention policy authorizes their disposal
Produce only the three years of logs the policy requires, since the policy defines the legal obligation
Negotiate the scope of the demand with the regulator before preserving anything

q: A newly hired business continuity manager is launching the organization's first formal continuity program. Which element is MOST critical to obtain before any other work begins?
c: A completed inventory of the organization's critical business processes
Signed contracts with an alternate processing site provider
A tested disaster recovery plan for the primary data center
Documented senior management commitment and a chartered scope for the program

q: A BIA sets the maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) for the order-processing system at 24 hours. The DR team proposes a significantly cheaper recovery solution with a recovery time objective (RTO) of 30 hours. How should the continuity manager respond?
c: Accept the proposal, because RTO measures data loss while MTD measures downtime
Reject it, because an RTO longer than the MTD means unacceptable harm occurs before recovery completes
Accept it, provided the recovery point objective stays under 24 hours
Reject it, and set the RTO exactly equal to the MTD so no recovery budget is wasted

q: An accounts-payable clerk has not taken a vacation in three years and resists all cross-training. Internal audit suspects the clerk may be concealing fraudulent transactions that require daily maintenance. Which personnel security control is designed to surface this kind of scheme?
c: Separation of duties
Least privilege
Mandatory vacations
Nondisclosure agreements

q: An organization is about to notify a systems administrator of involuntary termination. The administrator holds privileged credentials across production systems. From a personnel security standpoint, when should the administrator's access be revoked?
c: At or immediately before the moment of notification, coordinated between HR and IT
At the end of the administrator's final scheduled shift, to allow for knowledge transfer
After the exit interview concludes and all company equipment has been returned
Within 24 hours of notification, per the standard deprovisioning service levels

q: After a risk assessment, a hospital cancels a pilot program that would have let clinicians access patient records from personal phones, because the exposure cannot be reduced to an acceptable level. Which risk response does this decision represent?
c: Risk transference
Risk mitigation
Risk acceptance
Risk avoidance

q: A CISO must present emerging AI-related threats to the board next week. No credible loss history or actuarial data exists for these threats, but the board wants the risks ranked to guide funding decisions. Which analysis approach is MOST appropriate?
c: Quantitative analysis, because board funding decisions require monetary ALE figures
Qualitative analysis using expert judgment to rate likelihood and impact on defined scales
Deferring the analysis until enough incident data accumulates to compute reliable annualized rates
A Monte Carlo simulation seeded with published industry breach-cost averages

q: A security architect wants a threat-modeling methodology that begins from business objectives and impact, connects technical threats to business risk through seven defined stages, and produces output executives can use to prioritize spending. Which methodology BEST fits?
c: STRIDE
DREAD
PASTA
VAST

q: During threat modeling, an analyst breaks an application into its components to identify trust boundaries, data flow paths, input points, and privileged operations before any threats are enumerated. What is this activity called?
c: Reduction analysis
Root cause analysis
Attack tree construction
Gap analysis

q: An organization is negotiating with a SaaS vendor that will process regulated customer data. The vendor offers its marketing security whitepaper as evidence of strong controls. Which contract provision gives the organization the STRONGEST ongoing assurance about the vendor's control environment?
c: A confidentiality clause obligating the vendor to protect customer data from disclosure
A service level agreement guaranteeing 99.9% platform availability
An indemnification clause covering losses arising from a vendor breach
A right-to-audit clause with an obligation to furnish independent assessments such as SOC 2 Type II reports

q: A defense contractor discovers that network interface cards bought through a discount broker may be counterfeit and carry unknown firmware. Beyond replacing the suspect cards, which change MOST directly addresses the root supply chain failure?
c: Requiring firmware integrity scanning of all devices at deployment time
Procuring only through authorized distributors with a verifiable chain of provenance from the original manufacturer
Adding the broker to the vendor risk register and raising its assigned risk rating
Imaging and penetration-testing a sample of every future hardware lot before deployment

q: A year after launching a security awareness program, the CISO must show the board whether the program is actually working. Which measure BEST demonstrates the program's effectiveness?
c: The percentage of employees who completed the annual training module
Average scores on the knowledge quiz taken immediately after training
The trend in employee click and reporting rates across periodic simulated phishing campaigns
The number of awareness posters, newsletters, and events delivered during the year

q: A security program includes short monthly videos reminding all staff to lock screens and report suspicious email, role-based courses teaching administrators secure configuration skills, and tuition support for security degrees. What distinguishes the monthly videos from the other two components?
c: They are awareness activities meant to keep security present in everyone's mind rather than to build job-specific skills
They are training, because they teach staff how to perform specific security tasks
They are education, because they build long-term security understanding across the workforce
They are social engineering exercises that test staff behavior rather than inform it

q: A utility is defining protection goals for the SCADA system that manages a regional power grid; customer billing runs on a separate platform. When tailoring the CIA triad for the SCADA environment, which emphasis is MOST appropriate?
c: Confidentiality first, because leaked grid telemetry would help attackers plan intrusions
Equal weighting of confidentiality, integrity, and availability, since the triad requires balance
Confidentiality and nonrepudiation, so that operator commands remain provable afterward
Availability and integrity first, because the grid must keep operating and its control data must be trustworthy

q: After a major breach, the board asks who bears ultimate accountability for the organization's information security program. What is the BEST answer?
c: The chief information security officer, as the designated security executive
Senior management and the board, who own enterprise risk and answer for the organization's direction
The IT department, which implements and operates the technical controls
Each data owner, since accountability follows ownership of the affected assets

q: A global firm's monitoring policy requires recording all employee chat messages. Counsel in a newly entered country advises that such recording violates that country's employee privacy law, but security leadership insists the policy must apply uniformly. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Apply the policy uniformly, since internal policy takes precedence inside a private company
Obtain blanket employee consent forms so the recording can lawfully continue
Comply with the local law and adapt the policy for that jurisdiction, documenting the exception through governance channels
Suspend all monitoring worldwide until the policy and every country's laws are harmonized

q: A business unit cannot meet the corporate encryption standard on a legacy platform scheduled for retirement in 18 months, and remediation would cost more than the platform's remaining value. What is the BEST way to handle the noncompliance?
c: Grant a formal, time-bound exception approved by the risk owner, with compensating controls and a review date
Rewrite the standard so that legacy platforms of this type fall outside its scope
Reclassify the platform's data at a lower sensitivity level so the standard no longer applies
Leave the standard unmet but undocumented, since the retirement date makes the issue self-resolving

q: A regulation requires unique user authentication on a hospital's clinical system, but the vendor's software supports only a shared login and cannot be modified. The system is essential to patient care. Which approach BEST reflects sound risk management?
c: Accept the risk, since the requirement is technically impossible to satisfy on this product
Remove the system from service until the vendor adds support for unique logins
Declare the regulation inapplicable because the vendor, not the hospital, controls the software design
Apply documented compensating controls, such as individual OS-level authentication and monitored access logs, that meet the requirement's intent

q: A beverage company's competitive advantage rests on a formula it has kept secret for decades through NDAs and restricted access. An executive proposes patenting the formula for stronger protection. What is the MOST important trade-off to explain to the executive?
c: Patents protect expressions of ideas, so the formula would need copyright protection instead
Patenting requires public disclosure and expires after a set term, while a trade secret can last indefinitely if secrecy is maintained
Trademark registration would protect the formula while still keeping it entirely secret
Trade secrets become enforceable only after formal registration of the secret with a government office

q: The board of directors publishes a statement that the organization will pursue aggressive digital growth while accepting only minimal risk to regulatory compliance. A product manager then asks the risk team how much deviation from the approved risk level is acceptable for her specific product line before escalation is required. Which concept BEST describes what the product manager is asking about?
c: Risk appetite
Risk capacity
Risk tolerance
Residual risk

q: A risk analyst is instructed to evaluate the exposure of a new payment platform under the assumption that no safeguards or countermeasures are in place, so leadership can understand the worst-case exposure before selecting controls. Which value is the analyst calculating?
c: Inherent risk
Residual risk
Secondary risk
Acceptable risk

q: An enterprise risk register lists the CISO as the owner of every one of its 45 entries, including risks to manufacturing uptime, financial reporting accuracy, and third-party logistics. A maturity assessment flags this arrangement as a weakness. What is the BEST recommendation?
c: Retain the CISO as owner of all entries because the security function has the deepest expertise in evaluating and treating risk
Reassign each risk to the manager accountable for the affected business process, with the security team acting as an advisor
Transfer ownership of the register to internal audit so that risk decisions are overseen by an independent function
Assign ownership of all entries collectively to the enterprise risk committee so treatment decisions are made by consensus

q: A CISO wants a forward-looking metric that will warn leadership when the organization's backlog of unremediated critical vulnerabilities is trending toward a level that could breach the board's stated risk thresholds, so treatment can begin before an incident occurs. Which type of metric BEST fits this need?
c: A key performance indicator
A key goal indicator
A return on security investment calculation
A key risk indicator

q: An organization posts prominent signs stating that all warehouse areas are under continuous video surveillance and that violators will be prosecuted. The signs are intended to discourage theft before it is attempted. From a functional perspective, what type of control are the signs?
c: Deterrent
Preventive
Detective
Corrective

q: To reduce ransomware exposure, an organization deploys fully automated same-day patching to all production servers. Two weeks later, an untested vendor patch takes the order-processing cluster offline for a full business day. From a risk management perspective, the outage exposure created by the new patching process is BEST described as what?
c: Residual risk
Control risk
Secondary risk
Inherent risk

q: A database administrator legitimately holds the schema-modification rights required for the role, but can also open and read the plaintext contents of executive compensation tables that the job never requires the administrator to view. Which security principle is MOST directly violated?
c: Least privilege
Need to know
Separation of duties
Dual control

q: An attacker bypasses an organization's perimeter firewall through a misconfigured rule, but the intrusion is contained because network segmentation, host hardening, and egress monitoring each independently limited what the attacker could reach. Which security design principle does this outcome illustrate?
c: Defense in depth
Zero trust
Security through obscurity
Fail-safe defaults

q: A newly appointed CISO discovers that security initiatives have been selected informally by IT engineers based on technical interest, and an external review notes that security spending shows no connection to the company's strategic objectives. Which action would BEST address the root cause?
c: Pursue ISO/IEC 27001 certification to demonstrate that a formal security program exists
Procure an integrated GRC platform to centralize the tracking of all security initiatives
Request an increased security budget so that more strategically relevant projects can be funded
Charter a cross-functional security steering committee to prioritize initiatives against business objectives

q: For three consecutive years, an organization's risk assessments identified an unsupported internet-facing server as a critical exposure, yet leadership declined to fund remediation each time. After a breach through that server, plaintiffs argue that executives were negligent. The executives' failure is BEST characterized as an absence of what?
c: Due diligence
Due process
Due care
The prudent man rule

q: A U.S.-headquartered manufacturer plans to ship network appliances containing strong cryptographic modules to a new engineering office abroad and to give developers there source-code access to the cryptographic libraries. Which legal issue MOST directly constrains this plan?
c: Cross-border personal data transfer rules that require approved contractual safeguards
Export control regimes that restrict transferring cryptographic hardware and source code across borders
Data localization statutes that require citizens' records to remain stored in their home country
Import tariff and customs valuation requirements imposed by the destination country

q: A company discovers that a competitor is marketing services under a nearly identical logo and brand name, causing several customers to sign contracts with the wrong firm. Which form of intellectual property protection MOST directly applies to this situation?
c: Copyright
Patent
Trade secret
Trademark

q: A SaaS provider confirms that personal data belonging to customers residing in several countries was exfiltrated, and containment is complete. Notification deadlines, thresholds, and required recipients differ across the affected jurisdictions. What should incident response leadership do FIRST regarding external disclosure?
c: Notify every affected individual worldwide within 72 hours of confirming the breach
Engage legal counsel to map each affected jurisdiction's notification obligations, deadlines, and required content
Defer all external notification until the forensic root-cause analysis is fully complete
Notify the data protection regulator in the country where the provider is headquartered

q: An organization files a lawsuit against a former contractor seeking monetary damages for misappropriating proprietary data. The security team asks what standard the collected evidence must ultimately satisfy for the organization to prevail in this proceeding. Which standard of proof applies?
c: Beyond a reasonable doubt
Clear and convincing evidence
Probable cause
Preponderance of the evidence

q: After detecting repeated probing from a specific source, a security team stands up a honeypot stocked with realistic decoy data along the intruder's existing attack path. The intruder breaks in, and the recorded activity supports prosecution. The defense argues the evidence should be excluded because the team lured the attacker. Which principle BEST supports admissibility?
c: Entrapment, because the honeypot induced an intrusion the attacker would not otherwise have attempted
Enticement, because the intruder had already demonstrated intent to attack before encountering the decoy
Exigent circumstances, because the evidence would have been destroyed without immediate collection
The plain view doctrine, because the intruder's activity was openly visible to monitoring tools

q: During an annual governance review, a CISO finds that the draft enterprise data protection policy mandates AES-256 for data at rest and names a specific vendor's full-disk encryption product for all laptops. What is the BEST recommendation for the CISO to make about this draft?
c: Approve the draft as written, because naming exact technologies makes enforcement measurable and audits simpler
Move the technology mandates into a supporting standard and keep the policy as a high-level statement of intent
Reclassify the document as a guideline so business units can deviate when the named product is unsuitable
Rewrite the document as a procedure giving step-by-step instructions for deploying the encryption product

q: A business impact analysis concludes that the order-management database can tolerate the loss of no more than 15 minutes of transactions, yet the platform is currently protected only by a nightly backup. Which continuity metric is unmet, and what change does it drive?
c: The recovery time objective, requiring faster restoration procedures at the alternate site
The maximum tolerable downtime, requiring a shorter overall outage window
The recovery point objective, requiring near-continuous replication or transaction journaling
The mean time between failures, requiring more reliable database server hardware

q: While developing the business continuity plan for a chemical processing facility, the planning team debates what the plan's highest priority must be if a disaster strikes during working hours. Which priority MUST come first?
c: Protecting the lives and safety of personnel and the surrounding community
Preserving the integrity of financial and operational data
Restoring revenue-generating production as quickly as possible
Meeting regulatory incident-reporting deadlines for the event

q: A regional bank periodically moves employees among accounts-payable, reconciliation, and vendor-onboarding positions. Shortly after one such move, the incoming employee uncovers a long-running invoice fraud arranged by the previous holder of the role. Which personnel security practice enabled this discovery?
c: Separation of duties
Mandatory vacations
Job rotation
Dual control

q: A senior engineer with deep knowledge of proprietary algorithms resigns to join a direct competitor. Management is concerned about disclosure of trade secrets after the departure. Which offboarding measure BEST protects the organization while remaining legally defensible?
c: Withhold the final paycheck until the engineer signs a new, broader noncompete agreement
Hold an exit interview that reviews the engineer's continuing NDA obligations and confirms return of all assets and credentials
Send the competitor formal notice that the engineer possesses the organization's trade secrets
Retain the engineer's system accounts in an active state so activity can be monitored after the departure date

q: A development team has finished enumerating threats against a new application and now needs a simple, repeatable scheme to rate each one, considering factors such as potential damage, reproducibility, exploitability, affected users, and discoverability, so the worst threats are fixed first. Which approach fits this need?
c: PASTA
CVSS
VAST
DREAD

q: A security analyst places the adversary objective 'exfiltrate the customer database' at the top of a diagram, then decomposes it into alternative branches of sub-goals connected by AND/OR logic, assigning feasibility and cost estimates to each leaf node to find the cheapest viable path. Which threat modeling technique is this?
c: Data flow diagram decomposition
Cyber kill chain mapping
Attack tree analysis
Misuse case modeling

q: A critical SaaS vendor satisfies every security term in its contract, but a breach occurs at a hosting subcontractor the vendor engaged without the customer's knowledge, and the customer finds it has no contractual recourse. Which contract change would BEST prevent a recurrence of this blind spot?
c: Prohibit the vendor from engaging any subcontractors or third parties in delivering the contracted service
Increase the organization's cyber insurance coverage for losses arising from incidents at the vendor
Require the vendor to submit the results of its own annual penetration tests for customer review
Require security obligations to flow down to all subcontractors, with advance disclosure and approval of subprocessors

q: An organization's security education effort consists of one generic annual module taken by all staff. Developers continue to introduce injection flaws into applications, and service-desk agents keep resetting passwords for callers without verifying identity. What is the BEST improvement to the program?
c: Deliver the same awareness module quarterly instead of annually to increase repetition
Apply disciplinary consequences to employees who fail security assessments
Add role-based training that targets the specific risks and duties of each job function
Replace the training program with stronger preventive technical controls

q: A CISSP-credentialed consultant is engaged to produce an independent comparison of three security products and then realizes she holds a substantial equity stake in one of the vendors. Under the ISC2 Code of Ethics, what is the BEST course of action?
c: Disclose the financial interest to the client and offer to withdraw from the engagement
Proceed with the evaluation while making a deliberate personal effort to remain objective
Quietly sell the equity stake and then continue the engagement without informing the client
Complete the comparison but silently exclude the vendor in which she holds equity
